## Define a recipe without running it

```{r}
library(glyclean)
recipe <- glyclean_pipeline(
  normalize_total_area(),
  impute_min_prob(q = 0.01, seed = 42)
)
recipe
```

The recipe is an ordinary list, with one `glyclean_step` per call. Each step
contains exactly `function` (the function object) and `parameters` (a list).
The experiment is supplied only to `apply_pipeline()`. All step arguments must
use their full keyword names. Argument expressions are evaluated once when the
recipe is built; processing starts only when it is applied.

```{r}
original <- glyexp::real_experiment
cleaned <- apply_pipeline(original, recipe)
history <- get_pipeline(cleaned)
history
```

The existing abundance assay is replaced, not duplicated. The input object is
unchanged. The history lives in `S4Vectors::metadata(cleaned)$pipeline`; legacy
experiments use `cleaned$meta_data$pipeline`. Existing metadata is retained.

## Direct calls and automatic choices

Direct normalization, imputation, filtering, aggregation, CoDA, protein
adjustment, batch correction and site-sequence annotation also append records.
There is no need to wrap existing scripts in a recipe to obtain a history.

```{r}
manual <- normalize_total_area(original)
get_pipeline(manual)
```

The `auto_*()` functions record the concrete operations actually selected,
rather than a second automatic wrapper step. A skipped automatic operation
adds no transformation. Plotting and QC summaries do not add processing steps.

## Replaying a recorded analysis

```{r}
replayed <- apply_pipeline(original, history)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(cleaned),
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(replayed)
)))
```

Recipes and histories serve different purposes. A recipe can select methods on
new data. A recorded history captures resolved arguments and concrete choices
for replay on the **same original input**, with compatible package versions.
Recorded CoDA histories contain a lightweight per-composition plan: actual CLR
or ALR function, selected reference, parameters and the random state before the
actual transformation. This also handles ALR-to-CLR fallback and mixed sites.
They require the original feature/sample identities and order. Neither the
original assay nor intermediate assay matrices are stored in history.

Site-sequence annotation stores the sequences used, so replay does not depend
on a FASTA file still existing or a remote UniProt response staying unchanged.
A protein-adjustment step includes its supplied protein expression matrix,
which is a necessary external input rather than an intermediate assay.

Steps have package-version and RNG attributes in addition to their two fields.
Replay restores the caller's random generator and state, including on errors.
Pipelines can be saved with `saveRDS()` and reloaded with `readRDS()`.
As with other R objects containing functions, only load histories from trusted
sources. Preserve the original data and an R dependency lockfile alongside the
pipeline for long-term reproducibility.

Custom aggregation callbacks have their statically referenced lexical values frozen.
Dynamic lookup (`get()`, `eval()`, or caller/global-environment access) is rejected.
They must be self-contained: external side effects, mutable reference objects,
and recursive callback environments are unsupported. A history is not an
archive of external services or a substitute for versioning dependencies.
